conviction_note: Mild up-lean: alt-data traffic (+12.3% same-store visits) points to a comp above the 6-7% guide and Ross's beats have been bought 6 of 7 times, while the stock de-rated ~5.8% into the print against a softer sector; offset by a real bar already above consensus (whisper $1.91, UBS ~10% comp) and a Q4 guide that TJX's fuel-driven cut and warm-weather comment make hard to raise. p_up 58 x abs 8.0 = +1.28; findings sum +1.8, similar in sign and size.
bar: Company Q3 guide: comps +6-7%, EPS $1.75-1.83 (https://finviz.com/news/384306/ross-stores-reports-strong-second-quarter-sales-and-earnings-results, 2026-08-20). Street: EPS $1.82 / revenue $6.2B / comp 6.9% (Zacks via Yahoo, https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/curious-ross-stores-rost-q3-131505255.html, 2026-11-16); Investing.com has EPS $1.86 / revenue $6.23B (https://www.investing.com/news/earnings/ross-stores-earnings-in-focus-can-momentum-sustain-after-q2-beat-93CH-5039346, 2026-11-19), so the two estimate sources disagree by 4c, but the company guide anchors it. print_vs_bar_pct is on revenue: a ~9% comp against the 6.9% consensus implies ~$6.33B against $6.20B, about +2%.
positioning_check: Short interest ~3.1% of float, ~9.8M shares, 4.6 days to cover, down 401K shares on the latest settlement (Equibles summary, https://equibles.com/stocks/rost/summary, page as of 2026-11-04); ShortSqueeze shows 10.18M shares and 4.4 days as of 2026-10-25 (https://shortsqueeze.com/?symbol=ROST). Not crowded. Skew -10.46 vol points (25d put minus 25d call), so calls cost more than puts and the options market leans up. Put/call open interest 3.0. Straddle implies 7.18% against a median past reaction of 8.03%.

ROST underperformed the sector by about 3.6 pts over 5d and 5.1 pts over 20d. On TJX's print day (2026-11-18) ROST rose +3.3% while TJX rose +8.0% and BURL +5.5% (Yahoo charts).
expectations.vs_targets: Spot $223.5 against a consensus target of $273.21 (Investing.com, 2026-11-19, https://www.investing.com/news/earnings/ross-stores-earnings-in-focus-can-momentum-sustain-after-q2-beat-93CH-5039346), about 18% below. High target not found for November; Truist was at $290 on 2026-05-22 per Quiver (https://www.quiverquant.com/news/Ross+Stores+Slides+as+Recent+Analyst+Downgrade+and+Profit-Taking+Weigh+on+Shares). 16 of 21 analysts rate it Buy.

UBS (Jay Sole) expects a ~10% comp and an 11c EPS beat, and says investor conversations suggest 'the market expects a similar type of report' (Investing.com, 2026-11-19).

Stock +4.39% (baseline), the smallest positive reaction of the last four prints despite the largest underlying beat.

expectations.real_bar: For the stock to rise, the release has to show a comp of roughly 9-10% (not just the 6.9% consensus), EPS around $1.90 or more, and a Q4 guide at least held and ideally raised, despite the fuel cost TJX just cited.

next_guide.street_next_quarter: not found (Investing.com says analysts expect Ross to maintain Q4 comp +4-5% and EPS $2.17-2.26; no Q4 consensus figure found)
next_guide.company_current_guide: Q4 comps +4-5% against a +9% compare, EPS $2.17-2.26; FY2026 EPS $8.61-8.77 including ~$0.60 refund, ~$8.01-8.17 ex-refund (https://finviz.com/news/384306/ross-stores-reports-strong-second-quarter-sales-and-earnings-results, 2026-08-20)
next_guide.basis: Ross's pattern is to raise FY by the Q3 beat and leave Q4 roughly where it was. TJX's 2026-11-18 Q4 guide cut its margin for fuel, and TJX said warm weather was holding back early-Q4 demand. Ross does not hedge fuel. Together these argue for Q4 maintained at best, while the Q3 beat lifts FY.

findings.finding: Placer.ai measured Ross same-store visits up 12.3% YoY in Q3 2026, with gains near or above 10% in every month through October. Ross guided a 6-7% comp and consensus is 6.9%. In Q2, total visits up 16.4% went with a 10% comp, so the traffic points to a Q3 comp of roughly 8-10%, above guide and consensus but at or near the buy-side's ~10%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Comp beats have been bought: +8.41% on a 7% comp against a 2-3% guide (2025-11-20), +8.11% (2026-05-21, 17% comp), +4.39% (2026-08-20, 10% comp).
findings.why_not_priced: The data is public (3 days old) and UBS's ~10% comp call matches it, so it is partly in the whisper. But the stock fell 5.8% in the 5 days into the print and is 18% below the consensus target. If the market fully believed a ~10% comp, the stock would not have lagged XRT by 3.6 pts this week.
findings.independence: UBS's independent ~10% comp estimate (https://www.investing.com/news/earnings/ross-stores-earnings-in-focus-can-momentum-sustain-after-q2-beat-93CH-5039346). Management said on 2026-08-20 that August was 'encouraging' (separate finding). Proxy: visits are not sales, and the Q2 visits-to-comp gap was about 6 pts.

findings.finding: The real bar is above consensus. The Earnings Whispers whisper is $1.91 against $1.82 consensus and a $1.83 guide top; consensus has risen from $1.74. UBS says investors expect a ~10% comp, 11c-beat type of report. A print that only beats the 6.9% / $1.82 consensus can disappoint.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2's EPS beat (~$2.06 ex-refund against a $1.94 consensus, ~6%) bought only +4.39%, the weakest of the last four positive reactions.
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus figures sit at $1.82-1.86 and are what wire headlines will compare against. The buy-side bar is not in the published consensus, so a 'beat' headline can still fall short of what holders want.
findings.independence: UBS investor-conversations comment (https://www.investing.com/news/earnings/ross-stores-earnings-in-focus-can-momentum-sustain-after-q2-beat-93CH-5039346, 2026-11-19); independent of Earnings Whispers.

findings.finding: ROST de-rated into the print. It fell 5.8% over 5 days and 5.6% over 20 days, against XRT -2.2% and -0.4% over the same days. On TJX's beat day it gained only +3.3% against TJX +8.0% and BURL +5.5%. Spot $223.5 is 18% below the $273 consensus target. Some of the high bar has been taken out of the price.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The baseline shows 6 of 7 positive reactions. The only large negative (-9.85%, 2025-05-22) was the print where Ross pulled its annual forecast (https://stocktwits.com/news-articles/markets/equity/ross-stores-shares-plummet-as-it-pulls-annual-forecast/ch0QIlDRbqJ).
findings.why_not_priced: This is a price fact, so it is priced by definition. What it changes is the bar: a name that ran into the print would need more. If holders were still positioned for a blowout, ROST would have tracked TJX's +8% on 11-18 rather than lagging by 4.7 pts.
findings.independence: XRT, TJX and BURL charts (https://query1.finance.yahoo.com/v8/finance/chart/XRT?range=1mo&interval=1d, https://query1.finance.yahoo.com/v8/finance/chart/TJX?range=1mo&interval=1d, https://query1.finance.yahoo.com/v8/finance/chart/BURL?range=1mo&interval=1d). Quiver describes earlier pre-earnings de-risking (https://www.quiverquant.com/news/Ross+Stores+falls+5.5%25+as+investors+de-risk+ahead+of+upcoming+earnings+amid+ongoing+tariff+and-consumer-demand+uncertainty, undated).

findings.finding: TJX reported the same quarter (Aug-Oct) on 2026-11-18. Consolidated comp was +4% against a +2-3% plan, Marmaxx +2% (from +1% in Q2) with flat transactions, and the back half of the quarter was stronger. Merchandise availability was 'outstanding' and closeouts were increasing. No shift by income group. TJX rose +8.0%. The off-price channel was healthy and better-than-plan comps were rewarded.
findings.link: Direct competitor in the same channel: Marmaxx (T.J. Maxx/Marshalls) is the closest US analogue to Ross, with the same off-price apparel/home model, the same branded-closeout vendor pool and an overlapping value shopper. TJX's quarter ended 2026-11-01, Ross's 2026-10-31.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: ROST gained +3.3% on TJX's print day, about 40% of TJX's own move.
findings.why_not_priced: ROST has partly absorbed it (+3.3% on 11-18), then gave back 1.6% on 11-19. The read-through to Ross's own comp is still unproven. Marmaxx improving is also a competitive point, since Placer shows T.J. Maxx visits turned positive in September and accelerated in October.
findings.independence: TJX call transcript (https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/11/18/tjx-tjx-q3-2027-earnings-call-transcript/) and longbridge on the +11% intraday move (https://longbridge.com/en/news/306008293). Same event.

findings.finding: Next-guide risk: TJX cut its Q4 margin and EPS outlook (adj EPS $1.42-1.45 against a $1.49 street) explicitly for higher fuel, called fuel/freight 'the largest headwind', and said unseasonably warm US weather was holding back demand in early Q4. Ross does not hedge fuel, its guide 'includes current higher fuel prices' as of August, and its Q4 compares against a +9% comp. This makes a Q4 raise unlikely; a maintain is the base case.
findings.link: Same channel and same freight/fuel exposure. Ross's CFO said fuel is the largest part of freight and is unhedged (Q2 call). Same holiday quarter and weather exposure.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: In Nov 2025 Ross raised its Q4 comp guide to +3-4% and rose +8.41%. In May 2025 it pulled its annual forecast and fell -9.85%. The guide has driven the largest moves.
findings.why_not_priced: The market rewarded TJX's comps and looked through its Q4 fuel cut (+8%). Investing.com's preview expects Ross to maintain Q4, so a maintain is roughly the base case. The risk is a Q4 EPS guide below the street if Ross also lowers margin for fuel. Diesel has eased to $5.94 (11-16) from the $6.35 Oct peak, which softens this.
findings.independence: Ross's own Q2-call fuel language (https://www.investing.com/news/transcripts/earnings-call-transcript-ross-stores-tops-q2-2026-estimates-shares-jump-after-hours-93CH-4870582). Shares the fuel series with the diesel finding below, which lands on the Q3 margin rather than the guide.

findings.finding: Diesel rose after Ross set its Q3 guide on 2026-08-20. The EIA average was $5.454 the week of Aug 17 and peaked at $6.352 on Oct 26 (now $5.937). Ross's Q3 EBIT margin guide of 11.7-12.0% already assumed fuel-related freight pressure at August prices, and fuel cost 10bp in Q2. The extra cost is perhaps 5-15bp of Q3 margin, roughly $0.01-0.03 of EPS.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior ROST print turned on freight; Q2's 10bp fuel hit was swamped by a 205bp ex-refund margin gain.
findings.why_not_priced: Small enough to be covered by comp leverage. TJX's Marmaxx margin fell 110bp, mainly on freight/fuel, so if the market extrapolates that, Ross's margin beat could look lower quality than its sales beat.
findings.independence: FRED/EIA August series (https://fred.stlouisfed.org/graph/?g=1XTvU) and FleetOwner 2026-11-11 (https://www.fleetowner.com/emissions-efficiency/news/55417900/us-diesel-prices-fall-nationwide-as-trucking-fuel-costs-remain-37-higher-year-over-year). This is macro-to-company transmission; Ross confirmed it is unhedged but did not give a sensitivity.

findings.finding: Ross's reaction function pays for beats. 6 of the last 7 prints were up, with a median absolute move of 8.03%; Q3 last year (+7% comp against a 2-3% guide, Q4 raised) bought +8.41%. Ross has raised its outlook on each of the last three calls. The most recent, largest beat (Q2) bought only +4.39%, so the payoff per point of beat is shrinking.
findings.why_not_priced: A base rate, partly priced through the call-side skew. Reported here so the judges can weigh the name's pattern of buying beat-and-raise prints against the shrinking Q2 response.
findings.independence: The baseline's 8-K-timed reaction history (sealed file); Investing.com on the Q2 37% beat.

findings.finding: Options lean up: the 25-delta skew is -10.46 vol points (calls richer than puts) and the straddle implies 7.18%. Short interest is low and slowly falling (3.1% of float, 4.6 days), so no squeeze dynamic either way.
findings.why_not_priced: Skew is the market's own directional statement, so it is priced by construction. Filed so the judges see that an up-lean here agrees with the options market rather than fighting it.
findings.independence: Sealed baseline options block (Yahoo chain, 2026-11-19 18:12 UTC).

findings.finding: Price competition in off-price: Burlington is putting ~40% of its $55M tariff refund into sharper prices in Q3 (guiding Q3 operating margin down 60-80bp), and TJX said it lowered retail prices in some categories where competitors cut prices. Ross has said it expects only low-single-digit AUR increases. This is a mild pressure on Ross's merchandise margin and on the Q4 outlook.
findings.link: Burlington is the third national off-price chain, with the same low/middle-income value shopper and overlapping store footprint. Ross's dd's and Ross banners compete most directly with Burlington on price point.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior ROST print turned on competitor pricing.
findings.why_not_priced: Burlington's price reinvestment is known but its effect on Ross's margin has not been measured. Placer's +12.3% Ross traffic argues it has not cost Ross volume.
findings.independence: TJX call, on lowering prices where competitors cut (https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/11/18/tjx-tjx-q3-2027-earnings-call-transcript/).

findings.finding: TJX booked another $132M of IEEPA tariff refunds in its Q3. Ross booked ~$253M (~$0.60 EPS) in Q2, and its 10-Q says substantially all of it was received by Aug 1 without saying whether more is expected. If Ross recognises further refunds in Q3, reported EPS would jump above guide on a non-recurring item.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2's refund (+$0.60 EPS) came with a +4.39% reaction; holders appeared to look through it to the ex-refund beat.
findings.why_not_priced: Speculative and below the line; it would distort the headline EPS comparison against $1.82 but has no path to the guide.

findings.finding: On the Q2 call (2026-08-20, the last management statement found), management said August was 'encouraging' with momentum 'continuing to build', and Q2 exited on a 'very strong July'. The 6-7% Q3 comp guide was therefore set while seeing an accelerating August, against what management called significantly tougher back-half compares (Q3 compares against +7%).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Ross beat its own comp guide on each of the last four prints (comps 7, 9, 17, 10 against lower guides).
findings.why_not_priced: Three months old and known to the street; consensus has risen from $1.74 to $1.82 since. Filed as context for how conservative the guide is.

baseline_tension: The up-lean agrees with the call-side skew (-10.5) and the 6-of-7 positive reaction history, and cuts against the 5-day run-up, which shows the name being sold relative to the sector into the print. That makes the lean partly priced, so p_up stays near 58 rather than higher.
lessons_applied: Lesson 5 (proxy smaller than a company number): the Placer traffic finding cut from +1.5 to +1.2, because it is a proxy and Q2 shows visits overstating the comp.

Lesson 7 (sign against the skew): the next-guide negative cut from -1.5 to -1.2. A documented counterparty supports it, but it runs against a call-bid skew and diesel has eased since its peak; short interest is not crowded.
Lesson 2 (one-offs): the possible further tariff refund cut from +0.2 to +0.1, because it has no path to the guide.

Lessons 1, 6 and 8 left the rest standing. The reaction history shows beats being bought, so there was no veto. The bar is anchored on the company guide despite the $1.82/$1.86 consensus split. abs_move stays at 8.0, at the median reaction and above the straddle.
